name: Short Strangle
summary: Sell an OTM call and an OTM put in the same expiry; wide profit zone, high win rate, undefined risk on both tails.

legs.strike_rule: OTM call at 0.16 delta (the classic '16 delta strangle').
OTM put at 0.16 delta -- matched by delta, not dollars.

max_profit: total credit received, if the underlying finishes between the strikes
max_loss: UNDEFINED. Unlimited above the call strike; (put strike * 100) - credit below.
breakevens: call strike + credit per share, and put strike - credit per share

greeks.gamma: negative, less severe than a short straddle

when_to_use: IV rank > 50 in a range-bound underlying with no earnings inside the cycle. The canonical premium-selling trade, with roughly 70% historical win rates at 16 delta -- and losses that can exceed many winners when a tail arrives.
entry_rules: BLOCKED ON THIS ACCOUNT. Both legs are uncovered; this requires Level 4 naked authority. Alpaca provides Levels 1-3 only, and its multi-leg engine rejects any order whose legs are not covered within the same order. The router must refuse this structure.
Defined-risk substitute the system SHOULD trade instead: an iron condor -- the identical short strangle with long wings 1-2 strikes further out. Same profit zone, capped tails, Level 3 legal.
If it were enabled: IV rank > 50, 45 DTE, both legs 0.16 delta, no earnings inside the cycle, and sizing such that a 3-sigma move costs <= 10% of equity.
management_rules: If enabled: take profit at 50% of credit received.
Delta band: if either short leg's delta reaches 0.30, roll that side further out for a credit or close the position.
Never roll only the untested side down/up to collect more credit while the tested side runs -- that is how strangle sellers convert a manageable loss into a catastrophic one.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close whenever either short leg goes ITM with < 3 DTE, or whenever an ITM short leg's extrinsic < $0.10.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close the call side before any ex-dividend where the short call is ITM and extrinsic < 1.5 * dividend.
assignment_risk: Both legs can be assigned, and neither is covered. An assigned put delivers 100 shares per contract; an assigned call creates short stock. With no long wings, the resulting position is naked equity risk. This is exactly what the Level 3 restriction exists to prevent.
buying_power: Reg-T naked requirement per side, the greater side held plus the other side's premium -- typically $8,000-$15,000 per contract on index ETFs. Not available on Alpaca.
liquidity_needs: 16-delta wings on liquid index ETFs quote well; on single names they do not. Irrelevant here since the structure is blocked.
common_mistakes: Believing the high win rate is the whole story; not defining a stop; rolling the untested side; running it through earnings; assuming assignment can be 'handled later'.
zero_dte_notes: Not permitted (Level 4) and, at 0DTE, the negative gamma is extreme. The correct 0DTE short-vol expression on this account is a defined-risk iron condor or a single credit vertical.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
